subject: Request: Nexus Lite variant safety review and temporary pin coordination
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@nexus.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nexus Labs Procurement <procurement@nexus.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Nexus Lite (small) variant — request to onboard + ask to hold pin

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. Nexus Labs is ready to request onboarding of a small/low-latency variant of our Nexus Lite family (artifact attached). This variant (nexus-lite-v1-small) is intended for chat assistants with short contexts (<=256 tokens) and is quantized to int4 during export. High-level asks: 

- Can Redwood run a compatibility and safety review for this variant and confirm whether the current serving kernels support the int4 path?
- If compatibility checks require longer lead time, can we request a temporary pin on the variant (pin to nexus-lite-v1-small) during the evaluation window to avoid automatic rollouts to other variants?
- We can provide an eval report and a sanitized artifact.

Attachments: nexus-lite-eval-report.pdf, nexus-lite-artifact.tgz

Proposed timeline: evaluation start 2026-08-24, 7 business days for compatibility tests. Let us know if you need a different cadence.

Happy to hop on a short call this week to walk through the artifact.

Best,
Maya Rao
Head of Integrations, Nexus Labs
maya.rao@nexus.ai
[Attachment: nexus-lite-eval-report.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: nexus-lite-artifact.tgz (tgz)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@nexus.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexus Lite (small) variant — request to onboard + ask to hold pin

Hi Maya — thanks for the materials. Quick checklist from runtime/compat perspective so we can scope the work: 

- Exact model format (hf diff, ggml, pt) and quantization tool/version used for int4.
- Expected KV-cache growth per request (typical context sizes and concurrency).
- Maximum sequence length and batch patterns (p50/p95 sequences).
- Any custom ops or fused kernels in the artifact.

Can you also fill the attached compat-check-template.md and share the artifact download link (if different from the tgz)? If Nexus can run a small smoke test (100 requests) and provide logs, that accelerates our triage.

If there are no blockers, I agree with a temporary pin request until we validate. Tentatively proposing a 14-day pin window starting on approval.

Irene — tagging you for approval authority on temporary pin exceptions. Grace / Vivek — please weigh in on canary scope and monitoring.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: compat-check-template.md (md)]

From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@nexus.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nexus Labs Procurement <procurement@nexus.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexus Lite (small) variant — request to onboard + ask to hold pin

Dev — thanks, attached is the completed compat checklist and a public artifact URL. We used the Nexus export pipeline v2.1 -> int4 conversion via quanttool@0.9. No custom ops; only standard attention kernels and fused gelu. Typical traffic: median request 60 tokens, p95 180 tokens. KV growth is modest for this family.

Artifact: https://artifacts.nexus.ai/nexus-lite/v1/small/nexus-lite-artifact.tgz
Attached: compat-check-template.md (completed) and a short sanitized smoke log.

If you prefer a call to walk through the export steps I can be available tomorrow 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Maya
[Attachment: compat-check-template.md (md)]
[Attachment: nexus-lite-artifact.tgz (tgz)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-24T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexus Lite (small) variant — request to onboard + ask to hold pin

Quick infra note after a local reproduce of the artifact: 

- The model runs on our current runtime but the int4 code-path falls back to a slower reference kernel for some matmul shapes we exercise at p95. That increases tail latency under bursty traffic.
- No functional correctness issues observed in unit tests, but we did see a small token emission drift vs. full-precision baseline on one eval prompt (within tolerance).

Proposed operational approach: 
1) Approve a temporary "pin" to nexus-lite-v1-small to prevent automatic variant swap while we do full compatibility tests. Pin duration: 14 days.
2) Canary scope: 5% of production traffic (route only from Nexus account) + synthetic traffic at p95 seq lengths.
3) Required tests before unpin: throughput benchmark at target qps, 1k-sample regression evals, KV-cache stress test.
4) Monitoring: token-level latency histogram, error rate, and a small quality check using the Nexus eval set.

I can prepare the canary config and runbooks (draft attached). If leadership signs off, infra will schedule a canary job and gate unpin on passing criteria above.

Attachments: pin-runbook-draft.md

– Vivek
Principal Reliability Engineer
[Attachment: pin-runbook-draft.md (md)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Rao <maya.rao@nexus.ai>, Nexus Labs Procurement <procurement@nexus.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nexus Lite (small) variant — request to onboard + ask to hold pin

Thanks everyone for the rapid triage and clear plan. I approve a temporary 14-day pin for nexus-lite-v1-small with the following conditions: 

- Canary must be limited to Nexus Labs traffic (customer-bound only) and not a global rollout.
- Infra to run the 1k-sample regression and KV-cache stress within 48 hours of pin activation.
- Unpin only if all pass criteria in Vivek's runbook are green; otherwise Escalation to me and Product for rollback decision.
- Dev and Product/CS to document the expected customer impact and notify Nexus Labs of the canary window and abort criteria.

Dev: please add the pin to the onboarding board and schedule the canary job. Grace: coordinate on monitoring dashboards (token latency + quality check). Vivek: share the canary config and run the job. Maya: we appreciate Nexus providing the sample traffic and the eval set.

I will mark this as an exception and revisit after the canary. If everything looks good we can fold the variant into the model catalog.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
